title: Native registries fail to reject their exact capacity boundary
description:
`indigo_libs/indigo_client.c:209`, `:400` and `:530` test `empty_slot > INDIGO_MAX_DRIVERS/SERVERS`. Arrays are declared with exactly those capacities (`:75`, `:313`, `:441`; public header defines256 drivers and10 servers). With no reusable slot, empty_slot equals the used count, so the257th distinct driver or11th live remote server/subprocess bypasses the intended TOO_MANY_ELEMENTS return and indexes the element after the registry. This is an ordinary full-capacity contract mismatch; no capacity stress or malicious-input run was performed. Remediation: reject `>=` before any indexed access, preserving reuse of gaps and duplicate semantics; add bounded unit fixtures at capacity-1, capacity and after removal. Treat three registries together but do not rewrite unrelated connection behavior. Additional current boundary: indigo_bus.c:2470-2483 writes slaves[count] before count++ >= max, so zero/full capacity can index outside the caller-provided extent. Next: reject before writes and verify zero/full boundaries alongside registry limits.
